page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor using the x86_64 architecture, with 2.0 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 360.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU features dedicated allocation and includes hardware-level flags such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all scoring in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core performance is strong, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25% at 70594.44. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with both small-block cached read-only and large-block uncached read-only operations placing in the top 25%. However, text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression remain weak.

In terms of workload fit, the n1-standard-96 is suited for multi-threaded applications that can leverage its high core count and strong memory bandwidth, such as parallel software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations, which all demonstrate average performance. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, where performance falls into the bottom 10% to 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers high resource density for parallelized workloads, but the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a tradeoff of lower single-core efficiency compared to newer hardware generations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-96 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance from the N1 family, featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) on an Intel Xeon processor and 360.0 GB of RAM. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Performance benchmarks show a significant contrast: single-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench, whereas multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are strong, placing in the top 25%. The instance delivers average results for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression. It is best suited for highly parallelized workloads, such as software compilation, ray tracing, and database management, that can leverage its high core count and memory bandwidth, though it is less efficient for single-threaded tasks or LLM text generation.
